subject: general
question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 6% per annum, respectively. Sachin borrowed an amount of ₹460000 from each bank. Find the positive difference between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Sachin after 2 (in ₹) years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective difference in interest rates = 6% − 3.5% = 2.5% per annum

Total difference in simple interest for 2 years = 2.5% × 2 = 5%

Difference in amount = 5% of ₹460000

Difference = (5 ÷ 100) × 460000 = ₹23000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹460000

Rate of interest for Bank A (RA) = 3.5% p.a.

Rate of interest for Bank B (RB) = 6% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Principal = ₹460,000
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Bank A
 R = 3.5%, T = 2 yrs
 SI = ₹32,200

 
 Bank B
 R = 6%, T = 2 yrs
 SI = ₹55,200
 
 
• 
 
• 

 
 Diff = 55200 − 32200 = ₹23,000

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = (460000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = 4600 × 7 = ₹32200

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = (460000 × 6 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = 4600 × 12 = ₹55200

⇒ Positive difference = SI paid to Bank B − SI paid to Bank A

⇒ Positive difference = 55200 − 32200 = ₹23000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated solely on the principal sum, whereas Compound Interest accumulates on both the principal and previously earned interest. The formula for CI is CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)T − 1].

Difference Between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference between compound interest and simple interest on the same principal and interest rate is directly calculated using the formula D = P(R ÷ 100)².

Rule of 72

It is a quick shortcut used to estimate the number of years required to double your investment at a fixed annual rate of interest. The approximate time is calculated as Time ≈ 72 ÷ R.
